strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing headless.run.drive now derives a bounded accepted_completion route from current TaskCompletionAccepted evidence so callers can close a completed run without raw ledger interpretation.
Consumes the M51.1 AcceptedComplete state as the next state-machine boundary after Completed rather than treating completion as only a task-local fact.

Rust re-reads task and run evidence, verifies Completed terminal evidence and accepted-completion fingerprint ownership, and denies malformed or conflicting acceptance evidence before reporting the route.
Reuses bounded TaskCompletionAccepted ledger evidence and replay-safe headless drive checkpoints without duplicating TaskRunning or TaskCompletionAccepted events.
Returns bounded accepted_completion route metadata alongside existing headless drive closure metadata, without raw prompts, provider output, raw ledger payloads, paths, command output, or secrets.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: Existing headless.run.drive can surface a bounded accepted_completion route when the latest Completed task/run has current TaskCompletionAccepted evidence matching its terminal completion fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M51.1 recorded AcceptedComplete evidence, but headless run-control still required the caller to inspect task.run completion_acceptance or raw ledgers externally.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Autonomous controllers would keep polling or interpreting AcceptedComplete outside the Rust runtime, leaving Completed -> AcceptedComplete disconnected from headless closure decisions.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.8 checkpoint recovery, M51.1 acceptance evidence, and the M51.1 remediation because this phase consumes accepted state in headless.run.drive rather than creating or fixing acceptance evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing headless.run.drive result behavior and protocol validation without adding a JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The accepted_completion route is bounded control metadata in an existing execution result, not a report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust derives accepted_completion from the current latest completed task/run and existing TaskCompletionAccepted evidence, verifies the terminal fingerprint and verifier-gate context, returns a close_headless_run next action, and replays from drive checkpoints without duplicate mutations.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless caller can now decide that a completed run has reached the accepted-completion boundary from headless.run.drive alone, without ledger scraping or caller-side acceptance inference.
answers.milestone_progress: This completes the M51 connection from Completed to AcceptedComplete to a headless run-control boundary, leaving only a possible Product DoD stop decision or closeout.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M51.2 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a headless completion routing phase. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and that the manifest describes real existing headless.run.drive runtime behavior rather than a report wrapper.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive returns bounded accepted_completion metadata when current latest Completed task/run has matching TaskCompletionAccepted evidence
the implementation adds no new JSON-RPC method and no report/readiness/history/verdict/inspection wrapper
accepted_completion routing validates task id, run id, AcceptedComplete status, terminal completion fingerprint, acceptance fingerprint, and verifier-gate status against current ledger evidence
unaccepted, malformed, failed-gate, stale, mismatched, failed, cancelled, or non-terminal evidence does not produce accepted_completion route metadata
replay of the same drive checkpoint returns the same accepted_completion and drive fingerprint without duplicate TaskRunning or TaskCompletionAccepted events
VSIX validators accept the bounded accepted_completion shape and reject malformed fingerprints, wrong status, unknown raw fields, and raw ledger payload fields

RPC and ledger-derived metadata exclude raw prompts, provider responses, final responses, file content, stdout/stderr, command strings, environment values, raw request bodies, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, and secrets
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_routes_accepted_completion_without_duplicate_mutation validates accepted completion routing through existing headless.run.drive, replay stability, and duplicate-free TaskRunning/TaskCompletionAccepted counts.
Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_does_not_route_unaccepted_completion validates that a completed but unaccepted terminal task does not produce accepted_completion route metadata.
Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_rejects_malformed_accepted_completion_before_session_mutation validates malformed/conflicting accepted evidence denial before another headless session mutation.
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests validate accepted_completion result metadata, malformed acceptance fingerprint rejection, wrong status rejection, and raw-field rejection.

accepted_capability: Existing headless.run.drive consumes runtime-owned AcceptedComplete evidence and returns bounded accepted_completion route metadata for headless callers
safety_boundary: accepted_completion is derived only from current Completed task/run evidence and matching TaskCompletionAccepted ledger evidence
headless routing does not append TaskCompletionAccepted and does not automatically accept unaccepted completion
malformed or conflicting accepted-completion evidence fails closed before an accepted route is returned
route metadata contains only bounded ids, status strings, SHA-256 fingerprints, verifier-gate status, replay state, and next action
VSIX validates transport shape only; Rust owns routing policy
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No automatic acceptance of unaccepted completion
No provider execution, tool execution, verifier retry, patch apply, workspace mutation, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No Product DoD matrix or broad runtime modularization
rejected_alternatives: Adding a headless accepted-completion inspection RPC was rejected because existing headless.run.drive owns run-control boundaries.
Adding another acceptance ledger event was rejected because M51.1 already owns AcceptedComplete evidence.
Caller-side ledger interpretation was rejected because M51 requires Rust-owned headless control flow.
Broad runtime modularization was deferred so this phase remains a bounded vertical slice.
technical_debt: crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be split only in a cohesive future refactor.
M51 may still need a Product DoD stop-decision phase after accepted completion is routable.
M50.1 journey admission atomicity remains separate non-blocking technical debt.
next_capability_rationale: If this phase is accepted, M51 closeout should decide whether Product DoD stop authority is a final bounded M51.3 slice or belongs to a later milestone.
